about: What each kind of object offers to the editor's rules (Properties > Interactions): its outputs, what can happen to it, and its inputs, what a rule can make it do. An object's family is the one whose class is its nearest ancestor (editor/logic_catalog.py). outputs: how the game hears each one (editor/LOGIC.md) and the Tag its link waits for ({src}: the object, {option}: a computer's option; none: the link is watched or set off directly). inputs: whether the action needs an object (target). A family's first input is the one a new rule takes. The page's sentences for each id are in static/app.js (LK_WHEN, LK_VERBS).

families.note: They ignore Trigger: SetSeq moves them (floor), as SequenceTrigger does. 'any': it has reached a floor.
A body fires no event of its own.
Not a LaserTrigger: before, it fell in 'zone' and offered 'leave', which it never sends.
A camera fires no event: it only makes the AI alarm noise. spotted is watched (bPlayerSeen).
off: UnTrigger, a sound effect that plays again by itself (its More sounds' Repeats every) stops.
Their Event is a list of targets, not an output: hooking it would break them (UCLink.AimsItsEvent). Revision's MoreTriggers are each named: the editor may not know their chain.
Revision's: their Event is their targets too, and they are switched off (UnTrigger).
Revision's other MoreTriggers: they never send their Event when the player walks in, only untrigger it when he walks out.
Containers (crates, boxes): what they hold is their Contents, Content2, Content3; fillcrate picks it by chance.
A device hacked untriggers its UnTriggerEvent list: hacked takes a free slot (a keypad hacked is its right code).
Its declared outputs and inputs (Tools > Scripts, editor/scripts.py ports) come first.

about_v2: Version 2 adds the one vocabulary every view reads (static/logic-vocab.js, logic_catalog.py): each output and verb has its label (the menus and the 'When it...' / 'It can...' chips), its sentence ('say', after sentence.when: today 'When', 'As soon as' after the rename pass), its arguments by type, the verb that undoes it ('inverse'), the games it works in, its disclosure level and search keywords. 'say' is a template, or a list of {if, say} tried in order (the last has no if): {name} is a word of the sentence or an argument shown by its type ({b:amount}: by another type), [...] is left out when a value in it is empty, 'many' is the sentence for objects tagged alike, 'pieces' are named parts of 'say', 'labels' a label by the target's family. movers: the words of a mover by what it is (door, bridge, lift...). pairs: the first choices of Connect, by the family of the source and of the target, the first first (no 'when': the source's first output); asks: the fields a pair asks for.

types.line: a text the player reads: sentences quote its first 60 characters
types.goal: a goal's name: the same name gives and completes it
types.port: an input or output a script declares
types.look: a light effect's words: its colour, beep, exact
types.colour: the colour of a 'look' (red when it names none)
types.sound: a sound, Package.Group.Name: sentences give its last part
types.object: an object of the map, by name
types.place: a point of the map [x, y, z]
types.whole: a whole number as links.py builds it: empty is its default
types.amount: a whole number without its sign ('take 2 from')
types.number: a number: empty or 0 is its default
types.seconds: seconds: sentences give them only when more than 0
types.button: a computer's option, 0-3: sentences count from 1
types.percent: a share from 0 to 100: sentences give it with %
types.itemclass: an item of the game, Package.Class: sentences give its name
types.pawnclass: a character class of the game, Package.Class: sentences give its last part
types.items: items of the game and how likely each is, Package.Class:weight;...: sentences name them
types.song: a music of the game, Package.Song: sentences give its last part
types.hex: a colour, #rrggbb: sentences give its name
types.rule: a rule of the map, by its id

about_graph: Read by the Logic window (static/logic-graph-model.js). setsOff: the outputs an action makes its object say again at once, every time (no time passes: a timer stopped, a cutscene started, a script answering an input; 'output' is any output a script declares), so that rules setting each other off with no delay are found before Play. pieces: the logic's own nodes (edits.logic): each kind's inputs ('in', the verb input's port) and outputs ('out', the output's port) as a script's, 'many' making one per input or output of the item ({n}, its number) or per phase of its list ({name}), and what its live value shows. story: the Story's word for a rule's verb, where they differ (a Story action drawn as a rule's).
